What makes Pachycephalosaurus so amazing?

With its thick, round head, Pachycephalosaurus is a dinosaur whose name means "thick-headed lizard." It may have shown off its strength using its head.

Nature and science facts about Pachycephalosaurus

Pachycephalosaurus lived in North America about 66 million years ago. The dome of its skull was up to 25cm thick, yet its brain was only about the size of an egg. People used to think it butted heads directly, but recent research suggests it more likely shoved with its body or shoulders to show off its strength. The small bumps around the head are another distinctive feature.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How thick was Pachycephalosaurus's head?
A. The dome of its skull was up to 25cm thick. Yet its brain was only about the size of an egg.

Q. Did it really butt heads?
A. Recent research more strongly favors the possibility that it shoved with its body and shoulders to show off strength, rather than butting heads directly.

Q. How can we enjoy it at home?
A. Comparing with a video of mountain goats head-butting, and explaining its thick head by likening it to a helmet, are great.
